meaning: From Carcharhinus: Greek karcharias “shark” (from karcharos “jagged”) + rhinus, an old name for sharks (from rhine “rasp” or rhinos “skin”), both alluding to rough skin; -formes “shaped like”
description: The largest shark order, with well over 250 species. Most have a protective third eyelid. Reef sharks, tiger sharks, bull sharks and hammerheads all belong here.
